label: input f at step 0 or 1
explanation: Fires when the input token is f at the first or second original position (t = 0 or 1), and essentially nowhere else. Magnitude is set by position: f at t=0 gives the maximum activation (~1.78, constant, about 85% of the mass); f at t=1 gives a weak activation (~0.27-0.40 relative 0.15-0.22) that varies a little with the preceding token. It does not fire on f at t >= 2, on the delimiter, or on copy-phase steps (only 2 tiny copy-phase activations, on an erroneous f input at step 10, out of ~33k). It also does not fire on any other token at t = 0 or 1.

issues: Minor factual error in the explanation. The copy-phase exception is not an 'erroneous f input'. On the test split the one miss is in an L=9 sequence that starts with f: step 9 is <DEL>, so the input at step 10 is the model's correct echo of original token 0 (f), with activation 0.03 of max. The profile also shows all active steps have correct=1. It is negligible: 0.0% of activation mass.

All other claims check out. On the dev split, phase gives original 33416, delimiter 0, copy 2. By t, there are 0 activations at t=2..9 and only 2 at t=10. All activation mass is on in_tok=f. Mass share is 0.847 at t=0 and 0.153 at t=1. The max is 1.78 and the top examples are f at t=0 at 1.00. On the test split the predicate scored precision 1.0, recall 0.99997, F1 0.99999 and mass recall 0.999998, with 1 miss and 0 false positives.
The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate. No systematic counterexample class was found (by token, position, length or history).
